references.text: God promises Abraham to make him fruitful and numerous, and to establish His covenant with him and his descendants—the same promises repeated in Leviticus 26:9
Isaac blesses Jacob with promises of fruitfulness and increase, reflecting the covenant promises in Leviticus 26:9
God promises Jacob to make him fruitful and multiply, using the same language about fruitfulness and covenant as in Leviticus 26:9
God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and turned toward the children of Israel—a parallel to the promise to turn toward the people in Leviticus 26:9
God promises to love, bless, and make the people numerous if they keep His commandments—the same theme of fruitfulness and blessing as in Leviticus 26:9
Ezekiel prophesies about an everlasting covenant of peace where God will multiply the people and dwell among them—an echo of the covenant promises in Leviticus 26:9
God establishes His covenant with Noah and his descendants—the foundational act of covenant-making that Leviticus 26:9 looks back to
The Lord will give abundance in the fruit of life if the people keep His commandments—a parallel to the promise of fruitfulness in Leviticus 26:9
